headline: A familiar classroom, made interactive
intro: We recreated a university lab in virtual reality, then added objects that respond to a motion controller. The project connected spatial reconstruction with playful, tangible interaction.
context: University of Michigan · Extended-reality course project · Oct 2022
role: Co-developed the Unreal classroom and interactive scene with teammate Maxwell Zuber.

question.title: How does a room become a place to interact?
question.text: Reconstructing the classroom established a recognizable setting. Adding controller-responsive objects gave visitors a reason to move through it, approach familiar props, and explore what they could do.

steps.title: Recreate the space
steps.text: Built a virtual version of a university lab with its windows, computer stations, fixtures, and room layout.

steps.title: Populate the scene
steps.text: Added classroom props and custom interactions. The recovered archive includes a printer, violin, trash can, discarded math book, and piano.

steps.title: Connect action to feedback
steps.text: Implemented the team’s motion-controller piano interaction: touching a key plays a default note, while controller buttons select notes for a simple melody.

gallery.alt: An illustrated controller points at a four-tone piano diagram beside contact, button selection, and sound-feedback steps.
gallery.caption: A new interaction schematic based on the original write-up. The drawing explains the behavior; it does not reproduce the original piano geometry.

finding.title: Spatial fidelity sets up the interaction.
finding.text: The project paired a recognizable classroom with responsive objects. Its most concrete interaction story is the piano: a familiar object translates controller contact and button input into immediate musical feedback.

details: The original walkthrough remains linked. The lightweight browser demo is a later reconstruction using new geometry and generated oscillator tones; it is separate from the original Unreal build.
The recovered write-up documents the piano as a team contribution and describes playing Mary Had a Little Lamb. It does not divide individual component ownership.
credits: Classroom project by Le Qin and Maxwell Zuber. Scene assets and interaction behaviors are preserved in the original project archive.
The short clip retains the original prototype visuals. Its audio is omitted; the browser reconstruction also avoids reusing the original build’s credited film audio.
